html:
The Battle of Guam was the US recapture of the island from Japan in July and August 1944. US Marines and soldiers landed on 21 July and took the island within three weeks.

Japan had seized Guam right after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941. Its occupation was harsh: Chamorros faced forced labour, camps and massacres in the last weeks. The landing day is still celebrated as Liberation Day.

After the battle Guam became a huge base for bombers and ships in the last year of the Pacific War. Its role as a US base has lasted, and the Organic Act of 1950 followed.
